name: sph-dodec-half-split
comment: SPLIT COUNTERPART of sph-dodec-half: every edge that is exactly TWICE another carries a flat 180-degree corner at its midpoint, so one tile's side may be met by two. The dodecahedron edge 41.810315 degrees is exactly twice its half 20.905157, and the tile carries TWO of those full edges, so both are split. The mirror segment 69.094843 is not divisible and stays whole. Every tiling still uses exactly 24 of them. Halving a regular tile always produces this ratio — the cut lands on a midpoint, and arc length is additive along a geodesic, in H^2 and on the sphere exactly as in the plane (AL, 2026-08-18). The unsplit board sees only the tilings where every edge is matched whole; this one is a SUPERSET of it, so containment is the check to run. Angles unchanged apart from the flats, which is why the curvature is too: a flat corner adds D/2 to the angle sum and 1 to n, and (n-2)*D/2 grows by exactly the same D/2, so the tile's area is untouched. HALF THE DODECAHEDRON'S FACE, and the first half-tile here that is not a triangle. Three faces meet at every dodecahedron vertex, so the spherical pentagon's corners are 120 degrees. A pentagon has no diagonal that halves it — a diagonal cuts off a triangle and leaves a quadrilateral — so the cut is the MIRROR, from one vertex to the midpoint of the opposite edge, and the two halves are 60-120-120-90 QUADRILATERALS. Scalene and chiral. Its sides are the dodecahedron edge 41.810315 twice, half of it 20.905157, and the mirror segment 69.094843 — which is 90 minus the half-edge, exactly, and the long edge is again exactly twice the short one. Three edge types. D=12 because 30 degrees is one unit of 2pi/12; the angles are [2,4,4,3] and sum to 13 against the 12 a FLAT quadrilateral would, so the excess is 1 unit = 30 degrees = pi/6 and every tiling uses exactly 4pi/(pi/6) = 24 of them — the dodecahedron's twelve faces, halved. NOTE the arcs are DECLARED, not derived: a spherical n-gon has 2n-3 degrees of freedom against n angles, so a triangle is pinned by its angles and a quadrilateral is not.
